title: Generative AI for Humanitarians
html:
Generative AI for Humanitarians

With the hype cycle for Generative AI in full swing, it has become increasingly difficult to cut through all the noise, understand the current realities and identify immediate, practical use cases. Facing that challenge, Nasim Motalebi joined me earlier this year with the intention to better understand the technology, identify appropriate use cases, and produce a paper that would provide a concrete stepping stone for others to hopefully move forward more quickly. We are super excited to be able to share our paper today: Generative AI for Humanitarians.

The paper is aimed at humanitarian practitioners and leaders who would like to gain a general knowledge about Generative AI or would like to gain insight on trending strategies for mainstreaming these tools within their organization. By providing main topics of concern and recommendations, we laid out the landscape of capabilities and potential pathways for safe and responsible adoption of Generative AI.

[PDF]

Leveraging our conversations with a variety of people, from experts in the AI field to practitioners already implementing AI projects in their humanitarian organizations, we were able to explore possibilities and risks; document likely use cases; outline practical guardrails; explore various shortcomings; and provide recommendations for building an AI ecosystem. In the end, we hope that we have provided a practical report that others can use to kick-start their practical, yet responsible, adoption of Generative AI.

Andrej
teaser: A paper with Nasim Motalebi that cuts through the noise to give humanitarian practitioners and leaders a practical starting point on Generative AI.
seo_description: Introducing Generative AI for Humanitarians, a paper by Andrej Verity and Nasim Motalebi on the technology and practical use cases for the humanitarian sector.
